item.title: Volunteering at a charity run
item.context_text: You have signed up to volunteer at a 10 km charity run in a big city park on Sunday. Many runners are international students and visitors, so the volunteers work in English.
item.objective_text: Understand your role and a last-minute change, help a runner who gets hurt, and report back to the coordinator.
item.target_grammar: will and going to for promises and plans (I'll call the medical team. They're going to come.)
item.cultural_note: At events like this, volunteers are expected to follow the safety plan exactly. Staying calm and telling an injured person what you are doing helps them feel safe.
success_conditions: Understand your post, your job and the safety rule
Help an injured runner calmly and correctly
Report what happened and suggest an improvement

children.title: Read the volunteer briefing
children.instructions: Read the volunteer briefing. Then answer the questions.
children.prompt_text:
VOLUNTEER BRIEFING — Sunday Charity Run
Arrive at 7:15 am at the blue tent next to the main gate. Collect your orange T-shirt and a bottle of water.
Your post: Water Station 2 (the 5 km point, by the lake).
Your job: hand out water, keep the path clear and put empty cups in the bins.
If a runner is hurt or feels unwell, do not move them. Call the medical team on the radio (Channel 3) and stay with them until help arrives.
The run starts at 8:00. The last runners usually pass your station by 9:30.

options: At the 5 km point by the lake
questions.explanation: "Your post: Water Station 2 (the 5 km point, by the lake)."

questions.prompt: What should you do if a runner is hurt?
options: Take them to the blue tent
Call the medical team and stay with them
Give them water and let them continue
questions.explanation: "Do not move them. Call the medical team… and stay with them until help arrives."

children.title: Listen to the coordinator
children.instructions: On Sunday morning, the coordinator speaks to all the volunteers. Listen and answer the questions.
children.prompt_text: Morning, everyone. It's Jamshid, your coordinator. A small change: because of the rain last night, the path next to the lake is really muddy, so we've moved Water Station 2 about two hundred metres up the hill, next to the café. Also, we're short of cups, so please don't fill more than fifty at a time. Thanks, and have fun!

questions.explanation: "Because of the rain last night, the path next to the lake is really muddy."

questions.prompt: What is the instruction about cups?
options: Fill no more than fifty at a time
questions.explanation: "Please don't fill more than fifty at a time."

children.title: Help a runner
children.instructions: A runner stops at your station in pain. Answer her calmly: tell her what she should do now and what you are going to do.
children.prompt_text: Runner: Ow! I think I've twisted my ankle. What should I do?
children.goal: Keep the runner still, call for medical help and reassure her.

points.label: say you will call for help

children.model_answer: Don't worry, please sit down here and don't try to walk on it. I'm going to call the medical team on the radio right now. They'll be here in a few minutes, and I'll stay with you until they arrive.

children.title: Report to the coordinator
children.instructions: After the run, Jamshid asks for feedback. Write a short message: what happened at your station, what went wrong, and what should change next time.
children.prompt_text: Jamshid: Thanks for today! Anything I should know about Water Station 2?
children.goal: Report the incident and the problem, and suggest an improvement.
children.model_answer: Hi Jamshid, it went well overall. At about nine o'clock a runner twisted her ankle, so I called the medical team and they arrived quickly. We ran out of cups before the last runners came. Next time I think we need more cups, or maybe a second table.
